lines:
Added `shell::user_runtime_environment(explicit)` - it clones the caller's map and applies the existing `apply_user_runtime_environment` baseline, so explicit values win - and used it in `python_spec`. Host Python children now receive the same per-user runtime baseline as host shells (Windows: TEMP, TMP, USERPROFILE, HOMEDRIVE, HOMEPATH, APPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA; POSIX: HOME, TMPDIR, TMP, TEMP). PATH is still supplied by `prepare_command`, so `python_spec` adds none; absolute interpreter identity and `-I` isolated mode are unchanged.

Updated `python_adapter.rs` to assert the caller's `EXPLICIT=value` survives and TEMP/TMP are present (USERPROFILE matched the host when defined), and recorded the decision in the bound design element aworkit.capability_host.process_runtime. Linked tasks 201 and 202 to that element.

Verified: `cargo test -p aworkit-capability-host --no-fail-fast` exit 0 (python_preparation_preserves_frozen_interpreter_isolation_and_legacy_arguments ok, no FAILED lines); `cargo test --manifest-path desktop/src-tauri/Cargo.toml --lib` 622 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.

Not verified: as with task 201, the running Aworkit process needs a rebuild and restart before the fix is live; a real host Python child was not executed end-to-end (the live Python RSS test requires the public internet and is ignored).

`python_spec` in `crates/aworkit-capability-host/src/tools.rs` returns exactly the caller's `invocation.environment` (pinned by `tests/python_adapter.rs:30`). The desktop Python job passes an empty map (`desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/tool_loop/jobs.rs:224`), so a host Python child receives only `PATH` + the machine-scoped baseline from `prepare_command` and lacks `TEMP`/`TMP`/`USERPROFILE`. Python starts and imports fine (absolute interpreter, `-I` isolated mode), but `tempfile.gettempdir()`, `os.path.expanduser('~')` and child processes it spawns still fall back to `C:\\WINDOWS`, the same defect fixed for the shell in task 201.

Fix: add a `shell::user_runtime_environment(explicit)` helper that clones the caller's map and applies the existing `apply_user_runtime_environment` baseline (explicit values win), then use it in `python_spec` so host Python children get the same per-user runtime baseline as host shells. Do not add PATH/PATHEXT here: `prepare_command` already supplies PATH.

Verification: update `python_adapter.rs` to assert the explicit `EXPLICIT=value` survives and `TEMP`/`TMP` are present (and `USERPROFILE` matches the host when defined); run the capability-host suite and the desktop lib suite.

data.title: Give host Python children the per-user runtime baseline
